>> On Feb 19, 2008, at 1:43 PM, Noel Jones wrote:
>>
>>> Dennis Putnam wrote:
>>>> I'm not even sure how to ask this question but hopefully someone
>>>> will understand what I am talking about.
>>>> I have 2 servers on two different domains (a .com and a .biz).
>>>> Both are set up almost identically and the .biz server is a backup
>>>> for .com. The .biz server is really at a remote disaster recovery
>>>> site and is an open directory slave. One of my disaster recovery
>>>> tests is to make sure we can get mail via that server but at the
>>>> same time I can't really change the MX records just for the test.
>>>> What I am trying to do is send mail to the .biz server by using
>>>> the .biz address instead of the .com. Seems simple enough to me
>>>> (which is probably why I'm having problems). However when the
>>>> email is received by the .biz server it seems to be trying to
>>>> relay it somewhere (the .com domain?) so I get rely denied. I am
>>>> guessing this is because of the way the MX records are set up
>>>> although for the .biz domain there is no alternate MX records. So
>>>> my question is, how can I get this server to accept and deliver
>>>> messages to the local mailboxes, at least for testing without
>>>> changing my DNS?
>>>> Thanks.
>>>
>>> You don't give us much information to go on here...
>>>
>>> Postfix by default allows relay access when either:
>>>
>>> The recipient domain is listed in mydestination, relay_domains,
>>> virtual_alias_domains, or virtual_mailbox_domains.
>>>
>>>  - or -
>>>
>>> the IP of the connecting client is listed in the mynetworks  
>>> parameter.
>>>
>>> If you get a "relay denied" message, then none of the above are
>>> true or you've changed the defaults.
>>>
>>> http://www.postfix.org/BASIC_CONFIGURATION_README.html
>>> http://www.postfix.org/DEBUG_README.html
>>> http://www.postfix.org/DEBUG_README.html#mail
>
>
